Subject: POC trial planning follow-up & workload intake - AcmeHealth

Hi Alex —

Great to meet yesterday. As promised, a quick recap from our discovery and the next steps to get the POC scheduled and scoped. Primary goal is to validate latency & cost for your triage/chat summarization workload and ensure integration with your PHI-safe pipeline.

Success criteria (draft):
- Avg 95th-pct latency < 600ms for 512-token responses at expected concurrency
- Per-token cost <= $0.0008 (target; may adjust depending on model selection)
- No PII leakage; logs retained per Acme policy for 90 days
- End-to-end test with representative sample corpus and traffic profile

Requested from Acme for intake (please confirm or edit):
- Traffic profile: steady-state 5 RPS, peak bursts to 50 RPS for ~2–3 mins, expected daily runs during business hours
- Typical input length: 40–120 tokens; typical output length: 150–600 tokens (summaries vary)
- Concurrent sessions: up to 30 simultaneous streams during peak
- Auth method: inbound calls authenticated via mTLS (we will provide endpoint guidance)

Next steps / owners:
1) Acme to share workload sample + small test corpus and an anonymized traffic trace (Alex/Priya) — by Fri 3/6
2) Redwood to provision a dedicated POC config and share evaluation plan + success criteria doc (Ben/Marissa) — by Mon 3/9
3) Tech sync to finalize model choices, batching, and KV/cache strategy (Dylan + Acme infra) — schedule for week of 3/9

Attached: acme_poc_requirements.xlsx (template for workload/profile intake).

If any of the intake numbers above are off, please reply inline and we’ll update.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the intake values with a couple of clarifications from the engineering side:

- Steady-state: 6 RPS (we recalculated after yesterday)
- Peak bursts: up to 60 RPS for short windows (typically 1–4 minutes)
- Typical input: 30–140 tokens; typical output: 200–550 tokens
- Concurrency: we expect 40 concurrent active sessions for the triage flow, but only ~15 long-lived streams; the rest are short requests

We’ll attach a 12-hour anonymized traffic sample and a small corpus (10k rows) to the intake template. Priya will drop those in the Drive link by EOD Fri 3/6.

Success criteria look fine — one ask on latency: can we aim for 95th pctl < 500ms for the 200–400 token responses? That’s our internal bar for user experience. If that pushes cost too high, we can agree on a tiered target in the evaluation plan.

Also: can Redwood confirm how caching/prefixing would be handled for near-duplicate requests? We have many templates that are repeated with small slot changes.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Director, Product — AcmeHealth

Appreciate the updated numbers — that helps. We can target a two-tiered latency objective in the evaluation plan:
- Target: 95th-pct < 500ms for 200–400 tokens (benchmarking on the hosted/Dedicated hybrid)
- Acceptable: 95th-pct < 600ms if we need to trade-off cost for throughput during sustained bursts

On caching: Redwood supports prefix caching and request fingerprinting. For template-heavy traffic, we’ll recommend a small fingerprinting layer at the API edge (we’ll provide config snippets) plus a short TTL cache for repeated prompt prefixes. We’ll include cache hit expectations in the evaluation plan so cost forecasts are realistic.

Action items updated:

Will follow up after we get the sample.

Hi Alex / Priya —

Quick operational notes from the infra side:

- For the traffic profile you described (steady 6 RPS, peaks to 60 RPS, concurrency ~40), our recommended POC config is: Dedicated single instance pool (1–2 A100-equivalent GPUs) with auto-burst to a 2nd pool for short windows. That configuration keeps 95th-pct latency stable while enabling burst capacity.
- We’ll configure continuous batching with a 5–10ms max wait to preserve latency for short requests.
- Tokenization profile: we’ll run the sample corpus and provide average tokens/input+output; expect quantized model option to reduce GPU memory and cost with minor quality trade-offs for non-critical summarization tasks.
- Please include any compliance-specific logs retention needs in the Drive doc (we saw 90 days noted, if different we’ll update retention config).

I’ll include a checklist in the shared Drive folder with the onboarding steps: sample corpus, anonymized trace, API auth cert, and any redlines for production-like test data.

Marissa
